# Plan — Master Index & Doc Architecture

This document defines **how this planning set is structured** and how it will be executed. It is the entry point for any human or agent reading this repo.

## Project

- **Name:** `noAir` (GitHub repo `noair-movie-downloader`)
- **One-line purpose:** Self-hosted web app that searches movies/TV via TMDB, finds torrent/magnet sources via Prowlarr, downloads them with qBittorrent (Docker), shows live download progress, and plays the finished video in-browser (or hands it to the user's local player).

## Goal of this doc set

Produce a complete, unambiguous blueprint so that:

- A human can review the entire plan in under 15 minutes.
- An agent can execute the whole build top-to-bottom **without making design decisions**.
- Every task has a verifiable "done" condition.

## Doc layout

```
AGENTS.md                        # Project rules, commands, conventions — always read first
docs/plan/
  00-index.md                    # THIS FILE — overview, build order, locked decisions
  01-architecture.md             # System design: components, data flow, boundaries
  02-specs.md                    # Concrete contracts: API, data model, UI, providers
  03-tasks.md                    # Ordered, numbered milestones w/ acceptance criteria
```

## What each doc is FOR (and what it is NOT for)

| File | Contains | Must NOT contain |
|------|----------|------------------|
| `AGENTS.md` | Repo-level rules, run commands, edit conventions, pointer to this index | Project design decisions |
| `00-index.md` | Scope, goals, **locked decisions**, build order, conventions for the docs themselves | Implementation detail |
| `01-architecture.md` | Components, responsibilities, data flow diagrams, tech boundaries, what talks to what | Line-by-line implementation |
| `02-specs.md` | Concrete contracts: endpoints + payloads, schema, UI screens/flows, provider interfaces | Rationale, alternatives, opinions |
| `03-tasks.md` | Numbered tasks in build order; each with inputs, outputs, acceptance criteria | Design discussion |

## Rules for writing every doc

1. **Decisions, not options.** Every "we could use X or Y" becomes "we use X." No open choices left for the executor.
2. **Requirements + acceptance criteria, not prose.** Facts an agent can verify. No ambiguous adjectives.
3. **One fact lives in one place.** If two docs disagree, the doc that "owns" it wins (ownership table below). Cross-reference instead of duplicating.
4. **Precise naming.** All names are written exactly once in `02-specs.md` and reused verbatim everywhere else.
5. **No "later"/"TBD" in a doc that the executor reads.** Anything unknown is recorded in this file under Open Questions, resolved, then moved into the relevant doc.

## Ownership table (single source of truth)

| Topic | Owned by |
|-------|----------|
| Tech stack, scope, build order | `00-index.md` |
| Components and data flow | `01-architecture.md` |
| API contracts, data model, UI, provider behavior | `02-specs.md` |
| Milestones, task order, acceptance criteria | `03-tasks.md` |

## Locked decisions

| # | Decision |
|---|----------|
| D1 | Backend: **Node.js + Express 4 + TypeScript**. Single-user app, no auth. |
| D2 | Frontend: **React 18 + Vite + TypeScript**, React Router, **Zustand** for client state, plain CSS (no UI framework). |
| D3 | Database: **PostgreSQL 16 as a Docker service** (named volume), `pg` driver, schema run on backend boot. |
| D4 | Torrent indexer: **Prowlarr (Docker)**. One normalized search API; trackers (TPB, 1337x, etc.) configured in Prowlarr, not in code. |
| D5 | Downloader: **qBittorrent (Docker)** via its Web API v2. Backend polls it every 2s. |
| D6 | Metadata + imagery: **TMDB API** (free key). All poster/backdrop images proxied by the backend so the key never reaches the browser. |
| D7 | Realtime UI updates: **Socket.IO**. Server pushes a full downloads snapshot every 2s. |
| D8 | Playback: **play only after the file is fully downloaded**. qBittorrent writes in-progress files as `x.mkv.!qb` and renames them when complete; the backend never lists or serves `.!qb` files, so `stream_file_path`/`streamable` appear only once a complete file exists (inside a season pack, individually-completed episodes unlock early). Completed files are served over HTTP **Range** (`/api/stream/:infoHash`) for external players and browser-safe direct playback; `lib/streamPlan.ts` still routes browser-unsupported audio (→ AAC remux) and sub-4K HEVC (→ H.264 transcode) through ffmpeg for *completed* files, and 4K/UHD non-safe video to the external-player flow via the `movie://` scheme. Browser codec limits (H.264/VP9/AV1; no HEVC/.avi guarantee) still apply. `playinfo` also probes every audio/subtitle track for the browser-player upgrade. Packaging never re-encodes browser-safe AAC-LC audio (stream-copied) and runs renditions concurrently (S14); before packaging, Watch probes `mseProbe` codec strings and routes undecodable video (e.g. HEVC Main10) straight to the external-player screen. |
| D9 | Deployment: single `docker-compose.yml` with services `postgres`, `qbittorrent`, `prowlarr`, `backend`, `frontend`. Frontend served by nginx that proxies `/api` and `/socket.io` to the backend. |
| D10 | Cost: everything is free/open-source. Only required external account is a free TMDB API key; an **optional free OMDb key** (`OMDB_API_KEY`) enables portrait posters for the wide tiles (§4.6) — cards degrade to monograms when absent. |
| D11 | Testing: **Vitest** on the backend (unit tests with mocked providers); frontend smoke test via manual run in M4. |
| D12 | Magnet links: prefer Prowlarr-provided magnet; otherwise build from `infoHash` + 9 public trackers (list in `02-specs.md` §4.3). |
| D13 | LAN exposure: `frontend`, `qbittorrent` (Web UI), and `prowlarr` are all published on host ports (`0.0.0.0`). qBittorrent must have strong credentials (it has its own login); Prowlarr has no auth — documented risk accepted for a home LAN. `postgres` and `backend` stay internal-only. |
| D14 | TV browsing (v2): TV titles present TMDB **seasons/episodes**; contextual Prowlarr searches are whole-show (S3 no params), per-season (`?season=N` → season packs + episode releases), or per-episode (`?season=N&episode=M`). | D15 | Frontend visual language: **Netflix-style; black & white UI chrome over full-color artwork**. Left sidebar removed; fixed top header transparent at top that fades to a black gradient on scroll. Home = static cinematic brand hero + **16:9 full-bleed title-card tiles** (whole-card click, no captions/info icons) that bleed full-width with the rightmost card clipped to invite scroll; full-screen search overlay. Trailer metadata comes from TMDB `GET /movie/{id}/videos` / `GET /tv/{id}/videos` through the existing key — **no new key, no YouTube Data API, no backend storage** (`S15`). TV cards use the **series** trailer (per-episode trailers are not surfaced — TMDB coverage is sparse). The on-card presentation is **D20** (this entry no longer defines rendering). Best-source search runs only when the title owns no copy, is deduped + cached in the API client per context (~10 min), and lazily re-fetches after the last copy is deleted. Releases of one movie are **versions of a single library item** (`lib/versions.ts` pure helpers + `store/versionStore` persisted to `localStorage` keyed `movie:<tmdbId>`; default rule = most recently completed playable copy, tie-break higher resolution): My Downloads shows one card per movie with hover version chips; the Downloads page groups copies under `Movie · N versions` headers and labels each row `audio · quality`. Downloads persist `audioLang`/`audioMode` (idempotent `ALTER`, `S4`) so copies differing only by language stay distinguishable. TV keeps its episode layout and only reuses the panel for the active season pack; the C-DL1 confirm sheet is unchanged. |
| D20 | **Expanded Netflix-style hover card (replaces D18's inline overlay)**: every `TitleCard` expands into a **portaled, fixed pop-up card** after a sustained ~600 ms hover — width **1.7×** the base card (viewport-clamped), **vertically centered on the base cell (grows equally above and below)** and horizontally centered so it **overflows the neighbouring cards on all four sides**, `z-index: 150`, 8 px radius + strong dark shadow; base card keeps its grid slot (no white ring/scale while open); any scroll/resize dismisses it. Split layout: **media top (16:9)** = autoplay-looped trailer with **sound ON by default** (Chrome silences unmuted autoplay until the user has clicked the app once) + circular mute/unmute button that **remounts the iframe** (clip restarts), title/logo bottom-left over a scrim; **details bottom (dark column)** = compact Netflix-matching panel (16 px gutters, ~1.35 line-height, medium-500 13 px text): row 1 = Play (white circle → primary Watch action when present, else Detail) + two **decorative no-op circles** (Add to List `+`, Rate thumbs-up) + More Info chevron; My-Downloads version chips sit on their **own row beneath the actions**; row 2 = monochrome age-badge (`certification`) · duration ("2h 15m") or season count ("N Seasons") · `HD` chip (all 1 px translucent outlines, ~11 px); row 3 = up to three genre tags joined by `•`. Typeface is self-hosted **Inter Variable** (proprietary **Netflix Sans** is never bundled) standing in for the Netflix look. Every milestone must be independently runnable and verifiable before the next starts:

2. Core domain logic that has no external dependencies (unit-testable first).
3. External integrations one at a time, each behind an interface (TMDB, Prowlarr, qBittorrent).

1. Agent reads `AGENTS.md`, then this file, then `03-tasks.md`.
2. Agent works through tasks **in order**. Each task names exactly which of the other docs to read.

### S2 `GET /api/media/:id`
- Auth: none

### S16 `GET /api/media/:id/hover`
- Auth: none.
- Request: query `type: "movie" | "tv"` (required).

- Errors: `400` missing/invalid `type` or id; `502` TMDB unreachable. The frontend treats any failure as `null` (static card, no pop-up).

input.newString:
- Migration strategy: run `docs/../backend/src/db/schema.sql` on every boot inside a transaction (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`); no versioned migrations in v1. The schema file must **also** run idempotent `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` statements for any column added after first release (`backdrop_path`, `season_number`, `episode_number`, `audio_lang`, `audio_mode`, `art_files.imdb_rating`) so existing named volumes upgrade on boot.

### Table: `art_files` (D21 — portrait `poster` only)
| Column | Type | Required | Notes |
|--------|------|----------|-------|
| `media_type` | text | yes | `movie` \| `tv`; PK part |
| `tmdb_id` | int | yes | PK part |
| `kind` | text | yes | `poster` (the schema constraint keeps legacy `background`/`logo` values; new writes are `poster` only); PK part |
| `origin_url` | text | no | OMDb/Amazon URL the file was downloaded from |
| `file_path` | text | no | file name relative to `ART_DIR` |
| `status` | text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ok' | yes | `ok` \| `empty` (no poster found) |
| `fetched_at` | timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() | yes | |
| `imdb_rating` | numeric(3,1) | no | true IMDb score (`imdbRating`) captured from the **same OMDb response** as the poster (T-004); `null` until the poster pipeline/backfill has resolved the title. One decimal; `NULL` for "N/A" scores. |

- `ART_DIR` is a named compose volume (like `/downloads`, `/packages`) mounted at the backend's configured `ART_DIR` (default `/art`). Files are named `{mediaType}_{tmdbId}_poster.{ext}`.

part.text:
Done. T-004 implemented and committed on `ticket/T-004` (`127e97c`), working tree clean.

## What I changed

**Backend**
- `services/omdb.ts` — `fetchPoster` now also parses `imdbRating` (`"8.3"` → one-decimal number, `"N/A"`/garbage → `null`) from the **same** JSON response, so `OmdbPosterResult` gains `imdbRating: number | null` with **zero extra HTTP calls** and the budget counter untouched. Added read-only `isBudgetExhausted()` (consumption logic unchanged).
- `db/schema.sql` — idempotent migration: `ALTER TABLE art_files ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS imdb_rating numeric(3,1);`
- `db/artFilesRepo.ts` — `ArtFileRow.imdbRating`, selects/upserts include `imdb_rating` (upsert uses `COALESCE(EXCLUDED.imdb_rating, art_files.imdb_rating)` so a refresh never wipes a stored score), plus `listPosterRowsMissingRating()` and `updateImdbRatings()` for the backfill.
- `lib/artCache.ts` — `resolveOrigin` now returns a `PosterResolution { posterUrl, imdbRating }`; the warm upsert stores the rating for both `ok` poster rows and `empty`-poster rows.
- `lib/warmArt.ts` — one-time backfill `backfillMissingRatings()` runs with the warm loop (after the poster pass), re-resolving stored rows missing a rating inside the same daily OMDb budget; it stalls when the slice is exhausted and resumes on a later pass. Exported for tests.
- `routes/media.ts` — S2 detail and S16 hover payloads now carry `imdbRating: number | null`, read from the `art_files` poster row via `storedImdbRating()` (never an OMDb call; DB hiccup degrades to `null`).

**Frontend**
- `components/RatingBadge.tsx` — the single shared rating component (`★ 8.3`, `role="img"` `aria-label="IMDb rating 8.3"`, one-decimal). Renders nothing for a missing score.
- Rendered in the hover-card meta row (`TitleCard.tsx`) and the Detail-hero meta row (`DetailPage.tsx`, movies **and** TV). The Detail hero's old TMDB `voteAverage` star chip was removed (author chose IMDb only — scope-out). `HoverCardInfo`/`MediaDetail` types gained `imdbRating`.
- `styles.css` — one `.rating-badge` look used in both contexts.

**Docs** — `02-specs.md` (S2/S16 payloads, `art_files.imdb_rating`, migration rule, UI meta rows, §4.6 piggyback+backfill, canonical naming) and `00-index.md` changelog updated.

## Acceptance criteria verified (all Vitest, mocked providers)
1. Rating from the poster pipeline row appears on hover + detail for movie & TV, matching OMDb's `imdbRating` → `media.rating.test.ts`, `media.hover.test.ts`, `artCache.test.ts`, `omdb.test.ts`, `TitleCard.test.tsx`, `RatingBadge.test.tsx`.
2. Zero OMDb calls on hover/detail read of a cached row → `media.rating.test.ts` (spy asserts `fetchPoster` never called).
3. Backfill fills within budget and pauses/resumes on exhaustion → `warmArt.test.ts`.
4. No cached rating → no chip, no layout break, no throw → `TitleCard.test.tsx` + `RatingBadge.test.tsx`.
5. Migration idempotent (`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`), existing rows stay valid with NULL.
6. Same component/look across hover + detail, movie + TV.

## Checks run
- Backend: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` → 30 files / 294 tests pass.
- Frontend: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` (vite) pass; `npm test` → 17 files / 129 tests pass.

**Note:** `frontend`'s `ShakaPlayer.test.tsx` intermittently times out when the suite runs with many parallel workers on this machine (pure load flakiness — it passes standalone and the whole suite passes deterministically with `--maxWorkers=1`; that file is untouched by this ticket). No env files, `.opencode/plans`, or secrets were touched; nothing pushed.
